title: Pope John Paul II and Spring-Ford volleyball both reach the state semifinals
summary: Pope John Paul II beat Bethlehem Catholic in four sets Saturday for its 18th straight state playoff win and a fifth consecutive semifinal, while defending 6A champion Spring-Ford dropped the first set to Pennsbury before winning the next three for its 25th victory in a row. Both play Tuesday: the Rams against unbeaten State College at 5:30 p.m. and the Golden Panthers against Schuylkill Valley at 7:30 p.m.
loc: Spring-Ford and Pope John Paul II high schools, Royersford

title: Ricketts Center opens a gaming and technology room Nov. 19
summary: Boyertown Area Multi-Service will cut the ribbon at 6 p.m. Thursday on a room for coding, robotics and educational gaming for kids, plus computer classes for adults and seniors. The Pottstown Regional Community Foundation and Constellation paid for it, and a partnership taking shape with The Hill School would bring its students in as mentors.

title: Spring-Ford football reaches the district semifinals for the first time since 2012
summary: The fourth-seeded Rams beat Plymouth Whitemarsh 28-21 at home Friday night in a District 1-6A quarterfinal, improving to 11-1. Junior Rowan Harmon ran for 157 yards and two touchdowns, capping a 16-play, all-rushing drive in the fourth quarter. Next is a semifinal at top-seeded Downingtown East, which beat the Rams in week four.

title: Limerick weighs a $30 million community center in its main park
summary: The township is studying a 73,000-square-foot arts and recreation center in Limerick Community Park and has paid an engineering firm $140,000 for preliminary work. The idea dates to a 2016 plan for spending sewer-sale proceeds, and at the Nov. 10 budget discussion one supervisor argued the new comprehensive plan should come first.

title: Route 422 bridge demolition will close Sanatoga Road for three weeks
summary: PennDOT crews will remove the middle sections of the westbound Route 422 bridge over Porter and Sanatoga roads, closing Sanatoga Road around the clock between High Street and Linfield Road from Nov. 30 to Dec. 21. Porter Road gets daytime lane closures through Dec. 13, and the left lane of 422 closes overnight Dec. 1 through 3 as part of the $83.6 million rebuild of 2.1 miles of highway.
loc: Route 422 at Sanatoga Road, Lower Pottsgrove and North Coventry

title: Judge lets neighbors join the fight over the Pennhurst data center
summary: A Chester County judge ruled Nov. 10 that the owners of an adjoining 130-acre farm and the group East Vincent Advocacy may help defend the township's rejection of a hyperscale data center on about 125 acres of the former Pennhurst property. Supervisors unanimously denied the plan in May, and it stays denied while the developer's appeal proceeds.
loc: 1205 Commonwealth Drive, East Vincent Township (near Spring City)

title: Phoenixville filmmaker's documentary on domestic violence response screens at the Colonial Nov. 21
summary: Melissa Davey's third feature, Where Fear Ends, follows the Women's Center of Montgomery County from its 1976 start around a kitchen table to a network of seven offices and more than 150 volunteers. The center hosts the 1:30 p.m. screening on Saturday, Nov. 21.

title: Historical society opens an exhibit on 22 years of the Firebird Festival
summary: The new show at the Historical Society of the Phoenixville Area museum traces the festival from its 2004 start with design models, videos, fired clay birds and memorabilia, including the 2014 year when vandals burned the bird early and volunteers rebuilt it in days. This year's Firebird Festival is Dec. 12 at Reservoir Park.

title: Private club proposed for residential block of Gay Street goes to zoning board Nov. 18
summary: The 1978 Phoenix Foundation is asking the Zoning Hearing Board for a special exception to run a private club and community center, plus a variance for office use, at 315 Gay St. in the Residential Infill District. The hearing is 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Borough Hall, and the application can be inspected there.

title: Chicken Salad Chick sets Nov. 18 opening at Providence Town Center
summary: The Southern fast-casual chain's first Philadelphia-area restaurant takes the former Z!Eats space and will seat 55, with free chicken salad for a year promised to the first 100 guests. The local franchise group plans six locations across Montgomery and Chester counties.
loc: 500 Broad St., Providence Town Center, Collegeville
